once.soru: In what form does a plant store the extra food it makes by photosynthesis?

secenekler.neden: Glucose molecules join to form starch. Potatoes and wheat are examples of this store.
Glycogen is the storage substance of animals and fungi.
Cellulose is not a storage substance. It is the building material of the cell wall.

cards.p: Plants living on land faced the problems of drying out, moving water and reproducing. The cuticle reduced water loss, stomata controlled gas exchange and vascular bundles carried water. Pollen and seeds freed reproduction from depending on water.

ogeler: A fern has vascular bundles, but no seeds. It reproduces with spores.
A pine is a gymnosperm. Its seed sits exposed on a cone scale.

cards.p: Mosses and liverworts have no vascular bundles and no true roots, stems or leaves. They hold on with rhizoids and stay short. Their sperm reach the egg by swimming through water, so they live in damp places.

cards.key: Rhizoids mainly serve to anchor the plant. A moss absorbs water through its whole surface. Mosses, together with lichens, are among the pioneer species that first settle on bare rock.

once.soru: Why do mosses mostly live in damp, shady places?

secenekler.neden: For fertilization, the sperm must swim through water to the egg. Also, a moss has no vascular bundles to carry water.
Mosses carry out photosynthesis, so they need light.
Mosses have no true roots. They hold on with rhizoids.

cards.p: Ferns, horsetails and club mosses have xylem and phloem. They form true roots, stems and leaves. However, these plants have no seeds or flowers. They reproduce with spores.

A fern has no seeds.
These are the plant's normal reproductive structures.

cards.h: Alternation of generations: gametophyte and sporophyte
cards.p: A 2n cell has two of each chromosome, and an n cell has one. In alternation of generations, the 2n sporophyte makes spores by meiosis. A spore grows into the n gametophyte, and the gametophyte makes gametes.

cards.h: How did the dominant generation change?
cards.p: As you just saw, the gametophyte is dominant in mosses and the sporophyte is dominant in ferns. In seed plants, the gametophyte stays microscopic. Pollen is the male gametophyte, and the embryo sac is the female gametophyte.

cards.p: In seed plants, pollen is carried by wind or animals, so fertilization does not depend on water. A seed is made of an embryo, stored food and a coat. It can wait through drought and sprouts when conditions are right.

cards.key: A spore is a single cell. A seed is a multicellular structure made of an embryo, stored food and a coat.

once.soru: What advantage does a seed have over a spore?

secenekler.neden: A seed holds an embryo, a store of food to nourish it and a protective coat. A spore is a single cell.
A spore is a single cell, so it is much lighter than a seed.
A spore forms by meiosis, while a seed develops after fertilization.

cards.p: Pine, spruce, fir and juniper are gymnosperms. Their seeds sit exposed on cone scales. These plants have no flowers or fruits, and their pollen is carried by the wind. Most stay green all year.

cards.p: In angiosperms, the ovule is protected inside the ovary, and the ovary becomes the fruit. Double fertilization happens only in this group. One sperm forms the zygote, and the other forms the endosperm, the food tissue in the seed.

once.soru: Which part of the flower does a cherry fruit develop from?

secenekler.neden: After fertilization, the ovary becomes the fruit, and the ovule inside it becomes the seed.
The petals fall off after fertilization.
Pollen is the male gametophyte, and it does not become a fruit.

cards.h: Monocots and dicots: stems and leaves
cards.p: Angiosperms are divided by their number of cotyledons, or seed leaves. In monocots, leaf veins are parallel and vascular bundles are scattered. In dicots, veins form a network, bundles are arranged in a ring and there is a cambium.

once.soru: A plant has leaves with parallel veins. Which group is it in?

secenekler.neden: Parallel veins are a sign of monocots. Wheat, corn and tulips are examples.
In dicots, the veins form a network.
The cotyledon split is used only for angiosperms.

cards.h: Monocots and dicots: roots and flowers
cards.p: Monocots have fibrous roots, and their flower parts come in multiples of 3. Wheat and tulips are examples. Dicots have a taproot, and their flower parts come in multiples of 4 or 5. Beans and roses are examples. To identify a plant, look at several features together.

cards.p: Plants are the producers on land. They release oxygen and take up CO2. Their roots prevent erosion. They give people food, timber, fiber and medicine. Coal also formed from ancient plant forests.

once.soru: When the trees on a slope are cut down, which problem gets worse?

secenekler.neden: Roots hold the soil. When the trees are cut down, rain washes the soil away.
Plant cover does not affect earthquakes.
Other gases cause the thinning of the ozone layer.

cards.p:
• Plants are eukaryotic, multicellular, have cellulose walls and protect an embryo.
• Mosses are nonvascular and seedless. Ferns are vascular, but seedless.
• The gametophyte is dominant in mosses, and the sporophyte in all other plants.
• In gymnosperms the seed is exposed, and in angiosperms it is inside a fruit.
• Monocots have parallel veins and fibrous roots.

quiz.q: Put the life cycle of a fern in order, starting with the sporophyte.
ogeler: The sporophyte (2n) makes spores (n) by meiosis
The spore grows by mitosis and forms the gametophyte (prothallus)
The gametophyte makes gametes by mitosis
The gametes fuse and form a zygote (2n)
The zygote grows and forms a new sporophyte
quiz.e: The sporophyte makes haploid spores by meiosis, and a spore grows by mitosis into the gametophyte. The gametophyte makes gametes by mitosis. The diploid zygote formed by fertilization grows into a sporophyte again.

quiz.q: Sort each feature into monocot or dicot.
quiz.e: In monocots, veins are parallel, bundles are scattered, roots are fibrous and flower parts come in multiples of 3. In dicots, veins form a network, bundles are arranged in a ring and there is a taproot. Their embryos have two cotyledons.

quiz.q: The cells of a moss's green, leafy plant have 10 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in the cells of this moss's sporophyte?
quiz.e: The green plant we see in a moss is the gametophyte, and n = 10. The sporophyte grows from the zygote formed when two gametes fuse. That is why it has 2n = 20 chromosomes.

quiz.q: What is the main feature that sets a pine apart from an apple tree?
o: The apple's seed is inside a fruit, and the pine's is exposed.
The pine reproduces by spores, and the apple by seeds.
The apple has vascular bundles, and the pine does not.
The pine does not photosynthesize, and the apple does.
quiz.e: Both are vascular seed plants. The difference lies in how the seed is protected. A pine is a gymnosperm and has no flowers or fruit. An apple tree is an angiosperm.
y: A pine also reproduces by seeds. The difference is whether the seed is inside a fruit or exposed.
A pine is also a vascular plant. The main difference is whether the seed is enclosed in a fruit.
A pine has green leaves and carries out photosynthesis. The difference is whether the seed is exposed or enclosed.

bitki-biyolojisi.title: Plant biology
bitki-biyolojisi.summary: Plant tissues, how water and food are transported, plant hormones and reproduction

cards.p: The root anchors the plant in the soil and absorbs water and minerals. The root cap protects the tip of the root, and root hairs enlarge the absorbing surface. The stem holds the leaves up toward the light and transports substances.

once.soru: Which organ is the potato tuber we eat?

secenekler.neden: The eyes on a potato are buds, and buds are found on stems.
A carrot is a root, but a potato tuber is an underground stem.
A tuber is not a leaf. It is a stem that stores food.

cards.p: The waxy cuticle reduces water loss. The tightly packed palisade mesophyll carries out most of the photosynthesis. The loosely packed spongy mesophyll makes gas exchange easier. Stomata are mostly on the underside of the leaf.

etk.soru: Tap the numbers on the leaf section and see what each layer does.

noktalar.acik: The cuticle is a waterproof, waxy layer. It reduces water loss from the leaf.
The upper epidermis is a single row of clear cells. It lets light in and protects the tissues below.
The palisade mesophyll is made of tightly packed cells rich in chloroplasts. Most of the photosynthesis happens here.
The cells of the spongy mesophyll are loosely packed. The air spaces between them make gas exchange easier.
This is a leaf vein. The xylem on top brings water and minerals, and the phloem below carries away the sugar that is made.
The lower epidermis covers the underside of the leaf. In most plants, most of the stomata are here.
A stoma is the opening between two guard cells. CO<sub>2</sub> enters here, and O<sub>2</sub> and water vapor leave.

once.soru: In which layer of a leaf does most of the photosynthesis happen?

secenekler.neden: The palisade mesophyll has tightly packed cells rich in chloroplasts.
Epidermal cells usually have no chloroplasts.
The cuticle is not a layer of cells. It is a waxy covering.

cards.p: A tissue made of cells that can divide is called a meristem. The apical meristem makes the plant grow taller. The cambium makes the stem thicker by producing xylem toward the inside and phloem toward the outside. In seasonal climates, one annual ring forms each year.

cards.key: The bark of old stems is cork tissue made of dead cells. Flax and hemp fibers are sclerenchyma.

once.soru: Which tissue makes a walnut shell hard?

secenekler.neden: Sclerenchyma is made of cells that are hardened with lignin and mostly dead.
Parenchyma cells are alive and thin-walled.
Collenchyma is a living, flexible tissue. It is not hard.

cards.p: Xylem carries water and minerals from the root to the leaves. Its conducting cells are dead when mature. Phloem carries organic substances. Its sieve tube cells are alive, and the flow can go in both directions.

cards.key: Xylem cells are dead and carry water upward. Phloem cells are alive and can carry food in both directions.

etk.soru: Does each feature belong to xylem or phloem?
ogeler: In phloem, food flows from source to sink. The sink can be in the root or at a growing tip.

once.soru: Which tissue carries sugar from the leaf to the root?

secenekler.neden: Phloem carries organic substances from source to sink.
Xylem carries water and minerals upward.
The epidermis is a protective tissue. It does not transport anything.

cards.p: The root loads minerals into the xylem by active transport. Water follows by osmosis, and root pressure builds up. On humid nights, water drips from the edges of leaves. This is called guttation. However, root pressure is not enough to lift water to the top of tall trees.

once.soru: What causes the water drops seen on the edges of some leaves in the morning?

secenekler.neden: At night, when transpiration slows, root pressure pushes water out through the leaf edges. This is called guttation.
In transpiration, water leaves as vapor and no drops form.
The drops come from inside the leaf, out of pores along the edges.

cards.p: The evaporation of water through the stomata is called transpiration. During transpiration, water in the xylem is pulled upward. Water molecules cling both to each other (cohesion) and to the vessel walls (adhesion). This lets the column of water rise without breaking.

cards.p: A stoma is the opening between two guard cells. In light, K+ ions enter the guard cells, and water follows them. As the cells swell, the stoma opens. In the dark or during drought, the stoma closes.

cards.p: In phloem, food flows from a source, such as a mature leaf, to a sink, such as a root, a fruit or a growing tip. At the source, sugar is loaded, water enters and pressure rises. At the sink, pressure drops. This is called the pressure flow model.

cards.p: Hormones control growth in very small amounts. Auxin suppresses side buds. This is called apical dominance. Cytokinin stimulates cell division, and gibberellin stimulates elongation. Abscisic acid closes the stomata, and ethylene ripens fruit.

cards.p: A plant growing in response to the direction of a stimulus is called a tropism. The stem grows toward light, and the root grows toward gravity and water. A nastic movement does not depend on the direction of the stimulus. A sensitive plant folding up when touched is an example.

once.soru: A bee carries pollen from one flower and drops it on the stigma of another flower. What is this called?

secenekler.neden: Carrying pollen to the stigma is called pollination. Fertilization happens later.
Fertilization is the joining of sperm and egg, and it happens after the pollen tube grows.
Germination is when a seed starts to grow.

cards.p: After fertilization, the ovule becomes the seed, and the ovary becomes the fruit. A seed needs water, a suitable temperature and oxygen to germinate. Some seeds also need light.

cards.p:
• The apical meristem makes a plant grow taller, and the cambium makes it grow thicker.
• Xylem carries water upward, and phloem carries food in both directions.
• Water rises by transpiration pull and root pressure. Light and K+ open the stomata.
• Hormones control growth and tropisms.
• In double fertilization, the zygote is 2n and the endosperm is 3n.

quiz.q: The root cells of a plant have 2n = 14 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in this plant's endosperm cells?
quiz.e: The endosperm forms when one sperm (n = 7) joins two polar nuclei (7 + 7). That is why it carries 3n = 21 chromosomes.

quiz.q: Match each plant hormone with its main effect.
quiz.e: Auxin suppresses side buds, and cytokinin stimulates cell division. Gibberellin lengthens the stem and starts germination. Abscisic acid closes the stomata during drought. Ethylene, a gas, ripens fruit.

quiz.q: Match each plant movement with its name.
quiz.e: Turning toward light is phototropism, growing in response to gravity is gravitropism and winding around a support is thigmotropism. A sensitive plant folding up does not depend on the direction of the stimulus and happens through turgor. It is a nastic movement.

quiz.q: On the morning after a humid night, water drops appear only at the tips along a plant's leaf edges, and the drops contain minerals. What causes the drops?
o: A big increase in transpiration
Stomata staying open at night
Water vapor in the air condensing (dew)
Root pressure pushing water through water pores
quiz.e: This is called guttation. When transpiration is low, root pressure pushes mineral-rich water from the xylem out through the water pores along the leaf edge. Dew forms on every surface and contains no minerals.
y: In transpiration, water leaves as vapor, and transpiration slows in humid night air. The drops are caused by root pressure.
The water leaving the stomata is vapor. The drops that contain minerals are pushed out through water pores by root pressure.
Dew forms on the whole surface and contains no minerals. Drops seen only at the edge tips are guttation.

ekosistem.title: Ecosystem ecology and current environmental problems
ekosistem.summary: How does energy flow, how does matter cycle, and what disrupts an ecosystem?

cards.p: The interaction of living things (biotic) with the nonliving surroundings (abiotic) such as light, water and soil is called an ecosystem. From smallest to largest, the levels are the individual, the population, the community, the ecosystem and the biosphere.

once.soru: Which level do all the carp in a lake form?

secenekler.neden: The individuals of one species living in an area form a population.
A community includes all the species in the lake.
An ecosystem also includes the nonliving surroundings.

cards.p: The place where an organism lives is called its habitat. A habitat is like the organism's address. An ecological niche is the organism's role in the ecosystem, which is like its job. What an organism eats, when it feeds and which resources it uses determine its niche.

once.soru: Two birds live in the same tree. One eats insects by day, and the other eats fruit at night. What is different about these birds?

secenekler.neden: What they eat and when they feed, in other words their roles, are different.
Both live in the same tree, so they share an address.
They feed in different ways, so their niches are different too.

cards.p: Producers make food from inorganic substances. They do this by photosynthesis or with chemical energy, which is chemosynthesis. Consumers take in ready-made food. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead remains and return minerals to the soil.

cards.key: Consumers can be herbivores, carnivores, omnivores or scavengers. Chemosynthetic organisms get energy by oxidizing inorganic substances.

etk.soru: Place each organism by its role in the ecosystem.
ogeler: Cyanobacteria carry out photosynthesis, so they are producers.
It makes food from inorganic substances by chemosynthesis, so it is a producer.
A vulture is a scavenger. It eats dead animals, so it is a consumer. The organisms that break dead remains down all the way to minerals are the decomposers.

once.soru: In a forest, which organisms turn dead leaves into minerals?

secenekler.neden: Decay bacteria and fungi break down dead remains.
Producers make food. They do not break down dead remains.
Scavengers eat dead animals, but the ones that break them down to minerals are the decomposers.

cards.p: A food chain shows how food and energy pass from one organism to the next. Each link in the chain is called a trophic level. When chains connect to each other, they form a food web.

once.soru: In a chain of grass, grasshopper and frog, what do the arrows show?

secenekler.neden: An arrow is drawn from the organism that is eaten to the one that eats it. Energy passes in that direction too.
The arrow is drawn from the eaten to the eater, not from predator to prey.
The arrows have nothing to do with the size of the organisms.

cards.p: Energy enters an ecosystem as sunlight. At each level, most of the energy is lost as heat through respiration. Only about 10% passes to the next level up. So energy flows in one direction, while matter cycles.

cards.p: Substances that the body has trouble getting rid of, such as DDT and mercury, build up in tissues. Each consumer eats many prey, so the concentration of these substances multiplies going up the chain. This is called biomagnification. Top consumers are harmed the most.

cards.p: Matter moves through an ecosystem in cycles. The water cycle runs through evaporation, transpiration from leaves, condensation and precipitation. In the carbon cycle, photosynthesis takes up CO2. Respiration, decomposition and burning return CO2 to the air.

cards.p: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria such as Rhizobium turn N2 from the air into ammonia. Nitrification turns ammonia into nitrate, and denitrification turns nitrate back into N2. The phosphorus cycle has no gas stage.

cards.key: Decomposers turn the nitrogen in dead organisms into ammonia. This is called ammonification. Plants take up nitrogen mostly as nitrate. Phosphorus moves from rocks into the soil, and from there into living things.

cards.p: When fossil fuels burn, SO2 and nitrogen oxides are released into the air. These gases combine with moisture to form acids, and acid rain forms. Acid rain harms lakes, soil and forests, and it wears away marble.

cards.key: Normal rain is also slightly acidic (pH ≈ 5.6), but acid rain has a lower pH. Waste, fertilizers and pesticides also pollute water and soil.

once.soru: What is the main source of acid rain?

secenekler.neden: The SO₂ and nitrogen oxides released when coal and oil burn combine with moisture to form acids.
Ozone thinning is about UV rays, not acid.
Photosynthesis takes up CO₂. It does not produce acid.

cards.h: The greenhouse effect, climate and ozone
cards.p: The greenhouse effect is a natural process. CO2, methane and water vapor trap heat. When these gases increase, climate change begins. Ozone thinning is a separate problem. CFC gases weaken the ozone layer that protects against UV rays.

(1987)</text><path d='M6 156 H314' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-width='1' fill='none'/></svg>
cards.key: Fossil fuels and deforestation increase greenhouse gases. Glaciers melt and sea level rises. Ozone thinning is not the cause of global warming.

once.soru: What would Earth be like with no greenhouse effect at all?

secenekler.neden: If the gases did not trap heat, Earth's average temperature would be about −18 °C.
Greenhouse gases trap heat. Without them, Earth would cool down.
The greenhouse effect is a natural process and is needed for life.

cards.p: The eutrophication you just saw is started by the nitrogen and phosphorus in fertilizer. When plant cover disappears, soil is carried away by water and wind. This is called erosion. Habitat loss and overhunting reduce biodiversity.

cards.key: Invasive species also reduce biodiversity. They spread quickly because they have no natural enemies in their new home. The lionfish in the Mediterranean is an example.

cards.p: Species that naturally live only in one particular region are called endemic species. If an endemic species dies out in that region, it is gone from the world. About 80% of the plant species in Madagascar are endemic. Lemurs also live only on this island.

cards.key: Islands and high mountains isolate species, so they have many endemic species. The wild ancestors of wheat and chickpeas live in the Fertile Crescent.

once.soru: Galápagos giant tortoises live only on those islands. What are such species called?

secenekler.neden: An endemic species naturally lives only in one particular region.
An invasive species arrives in a new place and spreads quickly.
Pioneer species are the first to settle in a bare area.

cards.p: Sustainability means meeting today's needs without using up the options of future generations. The ecological footprint is the productive area needed for the resources we use and the waste we make. A smaller footprint is better.

cards.key: The main solutions are recycling, renewable energy, public transport, protected areas and international agreements.

once.soru: Which of these shrinks the ecological footprint?

secenekler.neden: Public transport cuts fuel use and emissions per person.
The more we consume, the bigger the ecological footprint.
The more waste there is, the bigger the ecological footprint.

cards.p: Waste management starts with preventing waste. We need to consume less and reuse things. The waste that remains is sorted at the source and goes to recycling, compost or the battery bin. A landfill is the last option.

cards.key: The right order is prevent, reuse and recycle. Burying is the last resort.

once.soru: What is the first choice in waste management?

secenekler.neden: The best waste is the waste that never forms.
Recycling is good, but it comes after preventing waste.
Burying waste is the last resort.

cards.p:
• An ecosystem is made of living things and the nonliving surroundings.
• Energy flows in one direction, and only about 10% passes to each level.
• Water, carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus move in cycles.
• Poisons build up going up the food chain.
• The answer to pollution, climate change and habitat loss is sustainability.

quiz.q: Put in order how a nitrogen atom moves from the air to a plant and back to the soil.
quiz.e: Bacteria fix N₂ into ammonia, and nitrifying bacteria turn ammonia into nitrate. The plant takes up nitrate with its roots and builds it into its proteins. When the plant dies, decomposers turn the nitrogen back into ammonia. This is called ammonification.

quiz.q: In a food chain, the producers store 50,000 kJ of energy. By the 10% rule, about how many kJ reach the secondary consumers?
quiz.e: 50,000 × 0.1 = 5,000 kJ passes to the primary consumers. Then 5,000 × 0.1 = 500 kJ passes to the secondary consumers.

quiz.q: Match each environmental problem with its main cause.
ciftler: SO₂ and NOₓ released into the air
quiz.e: SO₂ and nitrogen oxides form acids with moisture and cause acid rain. CFCs thin the ozone layer. Nitrogen and phosphorus from fertilizer cause eutrophication, rising greenhouse gases cause climate change and loss of plant cover causes erosion.

quiz.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: An energy pyramid is never inverted.
Ozone thinning is the main cause of global warming.
Like matter, energy cycles through an ecosystem.
Scavengers such as vultures are decomposers.
quiz.e: Energy is lost as heat at every level. So the energy of a higher level can never be greater than that of the level below. The other options are common misconceptions.
y: Ozone thinning leads to more UV rays. The main cause of global warming is greenhouse gases.
Matter cycles, but energy flows in one direction and is lost as heat at every level.
A vulture is a consumer that tears up and eats carcasses. The decomposers are bacteria and fungi.
